records.title: Advance Passenger Information System (APIS)
records.html:
Here is everything you need to know about Advance Passenger Information System (APIS) and how to update it on the PNR.

 

Policy

 

It is mandatory for all commercial airlines on international flights to send guest and crew manifest data to the Advance Passenger Information System (APIS). APIS details must be updated prior to departure to avoid delay at the airport.

 

The three SSR elements used for this purpose are categorized as:

  • DOCS: for the primary travel document information (e.g. passport or national ID)
  • DOCO: for the secondary travel document information (e.g. visa)
  • DOCA: passenger address information (either residence or destination)

The above three SSRs should be passenger-associated (mandatory) and segment-associated (optional). Certain countries require all three pieces of information to be inserted in the travel record locator of the guest that enters or leaves the country.

Note: The name of the guest is auto-populated. However, you should ensure that there is a space between the first name and title to avoid a name mismatch between the reservation and travel documents.

The UAE local authorities have informed that the submission of APIS must be precise and correct against the information of the travel documents.

 

Routes that require APIS information DOCS:

 

 

UK Inbound/Outbound KWI Inbound/Outbound
JFK Inbound/Outbound ORD Inbound/Outbound
LAX Inbound/Outbound ICN Inbound/Outbound
BAH Inbound JNB Inbound
CGK Inbound BNE Inbound
YYZ Inbound SYD Inbound
NRT Inbound NGO Inbound


For PEK: The 3 SSR elements of the API i.e. passport information (DOCS), destination address (DOCA) and visa information (DOCO) are mandatory.

 

For Japan: Authorities of Japan require APIS for all guests travelling to Nagoya (NGO) and Narita (NRT). Passport information (DOCS) is mandatory.

For Germany: DOCS SSR is mandatory and must be updated for all guests including infants travelling to Munich (MUC), Frankfurt (FRA) and Dusseldorf (DUS). Additional mandatory APIS data is required for nationals who require a visa to enter Germany. Incorrect or missing data may result in a fine of up to EUR 50,000.

For India: Passport information (DOCS) and visa information (DOCO) is mandatory.

UAE - name format

  • If the passport has two fields, one for ‘first name’ and one for ‘surname’, and one of them is blank/FNU/LNU, the other field must contain at least two words (names). 
  • If a travel document contains ‘XXX’ in one of the fields, it will not be accepted. 
  • Travel documents with two names added as observations/annotations or with a second name added on any page are accepted if the names belong to the guest or to the guest’s father 
  • This requirement does not apply to guests with valid UAE Emirates ID. 

 

UAE and Saudi Arabia - date of birth format

Passports with incomplete date of birth not as per the standard ICAO Format (i.e., 01/01/2010 Date/Month/Year) will not be accepted for entry into the United Arab Emirates or Saudi Arabia.

records.title: Animals and pets
records.html:
Live animals (restrictions apply) can be transported on Etihad Airways in the following ways:

1)    Pet in Cabin (PETC)

2)    Animal as checked baggage in cargo hold (AVIH)

3)    Manifested cargo

 

1)    Pet in Cabin (PETC)

Etihad Airways permits the carriage of following animals in cabin:

a)    Pet dogs or cats  (To be booked via Contact Centre only)

b)    Service animals (dogs only)

c)    Falcons

 

Guests with allergies and live animals:

Where a guest provides a medical report prior to the flight stating that they are allergic to animals, animals shall be accepted in the cabin according to the following specific conditions:

- In cases of a guest with an allergy statement and a guest with a pet request travelling on the same flight, the request of the guest who made the first reservation shall be confirmed.

- In cases of a guest with an allergy statement and a guest with a trained service animal on the travelling on the same flight, the trained service animal shall always take priority regardless of time of reservation.

 

Service animals and falcons:

- In cases of a guest wishing to travel with a trained service animal and a guest wishing to travel with a falcon in the same class on the same flight, the request of the guest wishing to travel with a trained service animal shall always take priority regardless of time of reservation.

Banned Breeds:

Following breeds of animals are not accepted on the aircraft:

-       Pit Bulls

1.    Staffordshire Bull Terrier breed of dog

2.    American Pit Bull Terrier breed of dog

3.    American Staffordshire Terrier breed of dog

4.    American Bully

-       Mastiff Dogs

1.    Brazilian Mastiff (Fila Brasiliero)

2.    Argentinian Mastiff (Dogo Argentino)

3.    Any Mastiff or Hybrid

-       Tosa - Japanese Tosa 

-       Rottweilers breed 

-       Doberman Pinschers

-       Canario Presa

-       Boxer

-       Any mixed breed of above breeds of dog or their hybrid

 

a)    Pet dogs or cats in cabin (PETC)

- Cats and Dogs are the only pets permitted to be carried on Etihad Airways flights.

- Pets are permitted to be carried in Economy and Business cabins only. Pets cannot be carried in the First cabin and The Residence.

- Pets are permitted on direct EY routes to, from or via Abu Dhabi on EY marketed (607 stock) and operated flights

- These are only bookable through Etihad Contact Centres

- Guests must be at least 18 years of age to be eligible to transport a pet.

- It is permitted for a guest to bring one (1) cat or one (1) dog as a pet in the cabin

- The maximum number of pets in the cabin per flight is as per the table below:

Note: Each pet must be in a separate travel kennel crate.

 

- On a flight with falcons(s) travelling in the cabin, a pet (dog or cat) cannot travel in the same travel cabin as the falcon(s). If a guest is travelling with a pet dog or cat in the cabin and another guest is travelling with a falcon in the same class on the same flight, the request of the guest who made the first reservation shall be confirmed.

- Where a guest with an allergy statement and a guest with a pet request are travelling on the same flight, the request of the guest who made the first reservation will be confirmed.

- If a guest travelling with a pet dog or cat in the cabin and a guest travelling with a trained service animal is on the same flight, the request of the guest wishing to travel with a trained service animal will always take priority regardless of time of reservation.

- The container (pet travel bag or kennel) must be within the maximum weight and dimension requirements for the applicable travel class (refer to sections 3.1 and 3.2) and must meet the following requirements:

o   The pet should be able to sit and stand in a natural position with its head fully erect (without touching the roof), turn around and lie down

o   The carrier must be ventilated on at least three (3) surfaces

o   The carrier must be escape-proof (rigid door for kennels / secure entrance for pet travel bag) and leak proof

o   The container floor must contain absorbent material

- The guest will provide:

o   Absorbent material for inside the container, including sufficient spares and disposal bags

o   Dry food in a sealed container for the animal, sufficient for the duration of the journey.

- The pet must not be allowed outside the pet travel bag or kennel whilst on board the aircraft.

- The pet must be of a minimum of 16 weeks old.

- In Economy Cabin,

o   For under-seat carriage, the pet must be able to fit in a pet travel bag or kennel with maximum dimensions of 40 x 40 x 22 cm (L x W x H) to fit safely under the seat.

o   For carriage on an adjacent purchased seat, the pet must be able to fit in a pet travel bag or kennel with maximum dimensions of 50 x 43 x 50 cm (L x W x H).

o   The pet travel bag or kennel shall be secured to the seat with extension seat belts.

o   The gross weight (pet and travel bag/kennel combined) should be no more than 8 kg.

- In Business Cabin,

o   It is not possible to stow pets under seats.

o   An extra seat must be purchased adjacent to the accompanying guest and the pet shall be in a pet travel bag or kennel with maximum dimensions of 50 x 43 x 50 cm (L x W x H).

o   Contact Centre agent must ensure that there are adjacent seats available on the aircraft and block them before accepting the carriage of pet request. If there are no adjacent seats, an alternate flight must be offered.

o   The gross weight (pet and travel bag/kennel combined) must not be more than 8 kg.

o   Where two (2) passengers travelling together wish to bring one (1) pet each (i.e., two (2) pets in total) in Business, an additional seat shall be purchased for each pet.

o   Where an additional seat has been purchased, the passenger is entitled to the additional checked baggage allowance associated with the purchased seat.

- Where possible, the guest travelling with a pet should be allocated a window seat. A guest travelling with a pet will not be seated in any of the following locations:

o   Bulkhead rows

o   Emergency exit rows

o   One row forward and aft of over-wing exit rows

- Standard Seat will be provided free of charge for a guest travelling with a pet (SSR PETC) within 48 hours of departure.

- Guests must submit the booking form at least 7 days in advance and provide all necessary documents to the Contact Centre no later than 72 hours prior to intended travel. Where three (3) pets will be carried as permitted, a separate form must be completed for each pet

- SSR PETC can be updated in the booking only by EY agents and it must be updated only after receiving all approvals

-   For guests using the Etihad Chauffeur service, or connecting Etihad Shuttle services in the UAE, pets are permitted on these services in accordance with this policy

-   For guests eligible to use premium lounges, pets may be taken into Etihad lounges in Abu Dhabi. For lounges in network airports, access is dependent upon the acceptance policy of the lounge operator. Pets must always remain inside the pet carrier or kennel
 
Terms & Conditions:
- Etihad Airways will not be responsible if authorities in other countries refuse entry of your pet due to non-compliance with local regulations. Etihad will in this case, not be liable for any resulting costs such as flight rebooking charges, hotel accommodation if Etihad have to refuse the carriage of your pet due to non-compliance with the regulations
- We assume no liability for the health or wellbeing of pets carried in the cabin
- The pet must be able to sit and stand in a natural position with its head fully erect (without touching the roof), turn around and lie down
- The carrier must be ventilated on at least three (3) surfaces
- The carrier must be escape-proof (rigid door for kennels or secure entrance for pet travel bag) and leak-proof
- The container floor must contain absorbent material
- You are responsible for additional costs for import or export
- Pregnant pets cannot be accepted for travel
- Guest must report 3 hours prior to departure at the airport
- Guest must bring enough of absorbent sheets for their pet to relieve itself, including connecting flights and transit airport, if applicable
- Guest can only carry dry pet food in your cabin baggage. Food should be carried in a sealed container so the smell does not disturb other guests
- If there are guests travelling on-board that are allergic to animals, our crew may be required to re-seat you and your pet. In rare occurrences, we may need to re-book your flight
- Sedation of animals, except under certain conditions and carried out under veterinary supervision, is not recommended. Commonly used tranquilizers lower blood pressure, which also occurs at high altitude
- The combination of high altitude and medicines could be dangerous for old, chronically sick or stressed animals. Keeping a container in a dark, cool, quiet place prior to flying will calm down most animals. If you have to sedate your pet per veterinarian’s instruction, the name of the drug and time of intake must be clearly marked on the container
- Pets must always remain in their carriers
- Guests must complete all formalities upon arrival at Abu Dhabi airport according to UAE regulations, including an inspection by the Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE) veterinary officer, performed in the Customs clearance area
- For all other destinations, guests must complete all arrival formalities according to local regulations
- Inspection and clearance areas may vary from airport to airport, guests must check with the applicable authority at their destination for specific requirements

 

Changes and Refunds:

Voluntary changes: The guest can change the request anytime up to 3 hours to departure time. However, if the guest wishes to take the pet on the new dates/flight, they’d need to inform Etihad Airways and go through the approval process again. The guest will still be liable of ensuring that the required documents, certificates, permits allow for the pet to travel on the rebooked flight.  The same process applies to guests who wish to upgrade their ticket to a higher class of travel. 

 

Involuntary changes: Etihad Airways will coordinate with the guest and provide the best available options in cases where the flight has been re-booked or cancelled. For delays or flight cancellations, the guest may utilize the original animal documentation.

 

Refunds: A full refund is only given for cases where Etihad had an irregular operation and was not able to transport the pet. In this case, the guest can reach out to our contact centers and request for a refund to the fees that were paid. The guest can request for a full refund for the fees that were paid for transporting the pet if the options that Etihad Airways have provided does not meet their needs, provided that the pet was not transported from the country of origin. If Etihad Airways was able to transport the pet on another flight/date or even airline after obtaining the guest’s consent, then refund is not allowed.

Special requirements:

 

1.    Malaysia:

For guests travelling with Pets (PETC) and service dogs to/from Malaysia, the below conditions apply:

-       Only small size pets and service dogs (up to 8kg) are permitted

-       Pets and service dogs must always be kept in a cage

-       Airport authorities reserve the right to stop pets and service dogs from passing through the airport terminal if they display inappropriate behavior

 

2.    Bahrain:

Bahrain airports will only accept pets that do not exceed 6Kg (including the carrier)

 

3.    Ireland:

Pre-notification of any PETC into Ireland must be sent at least 24 hours in advance of arrival via email to petmove@agriculture.gov.ie.

 

To book, please contact Etihad Cargo:

Email: LiveAnimals@etihad.ae

Phone: 800 2535 (within UAE) / +971 2 599 0099 (overseas)

 

b)  Service Animals (dogs only):

This policy is applicable to service animals. A service animal is defined as a dog, regardless of breed or type, which is individually trained to do work or perform tasks for the benefit of a qualified individual with a disability, including a physical, sensory, psychiatric, intellectual, or other mental disability.

 

The following are not considered as service animals:

1.    Animal species other than dogs

2.    Emotional support animals

3.    Comfort animals

4.    Companionship animals

5.    Service animals in training

 

-       Service animals will be accepted free of charge only if they are certified by ADI or IGDF accredited organizations. Only exceptions are guests travelling to/from the USA due to legal requirements.

-       Trained service animals must be trained to behave properly in public. The dog must be harnessed, leashed or tethered at all times. They will not be accepted in the cabin if they display any form of disruptive behaviour which may include:

o   Growling

o   Biting

o   Jumping on other guests or staff

o   Relieving at the gate or cabin

o   Causing damage to the cabin e.g. eating of the seatback

-       Guest must request and provide necessary documents to the Contact Centre no later than 48 hours prior to intended travel

-       There is no weight limitation for service animal except for Malaysia (up to 8kg)

-       The carriage of a service animal in the cabin is permitted on direct EY routes to, from and via Abu Dhabi (i.e. direct transfer)

-       It is permitted for a passenger to travel with one (1) service animal in the cabin

-       On any flight with falcon(s) travelling in the cabin, a service animal shall not travel in the same travel class as the falcon(s)

-       The guest shall provide an absorbent mat to be placed on the floor where the animal will be located and sufficient additional material for the duration of the flight(s) and, where applicable, transfer time

-       Where possible, the guest travelling with a service dog should be allocated a bulkhead row and a window seat. Seat will be provided free of charge for a guest travelling with a service animal (SSR SVAN). A guest travelling with a service dog must not be seated in any of the following locations:

o   Emergency exit rows

o   One row forward and aft of over-wing exit rows

-       Service dogs shall remain leashed, harnessed, or otherwise tied at all times. 

-       There is no charge for the carriage of a service animal in the cabin

 

 

 Pets and Service Animals

Details are available on the ey.com website. Alternately, guests can call the Contact Centre to enquire regarding travel with a pet or service animal.

Upon receiving a request for carriage of pet in cabin, Guest Contact Centre shall ask some qualifying questions to the guest due to restrictions which may disqualify the carriage of the animal. If any of the below requirements are not met, the guest shall immediately be advised that their animal does not meet the requirements for carriage and to contact Cargo Contact Centre (CCC).

i.        Is the animal a trained service dog? If yes, then the Live Animal in Cabin Information Form must be sent to the guest.

ii.        For pet cats and dogs, is the animal aged over 16 weeks? If no, then the pet will be rejected (not applicable to service animals)

iii.        What is the breed of the pet? If the breed is on banned list, then the pet will be rejected (not applicable to service animals)

iv.        What is the weight of the pet including the container? If more than 8 kg, the pet will be rejected (not applicable to service animals except for Malaysia)

v.        What are the dimensions of the pet container? (not applicable to service animals)

  • Economy: if more than 40 x 40 x 22 (L x W x H), the pet will be rejected.
  • Business: if more than 50 x 43 x 50 cm (L x W x H), the pet will be rejected.

If the above conditions are satisfied, Contact Centre staff will provide the guest with:

1.    Live Animal in Cabin Information Form

2.    Application Form for Trained Service Dog in Cabin (except where the itinerary includes a flight to and/or from the US)

The guest must be advised to email the completed form with the supporting documents to ContactCentre@etihad.ae, no later than 5 days prior to intended travel.

 

Supporting documents:

i.        Pet microchip number - must be completed prior to rabies vaccination.

ii.        Health Certificate – to be signed by origin approved/government Veterinarian.

iii.        Fit to travel certificate - from local vet within 10 days of travel.

iv.        Vaccination certificate with all vaccines and treatments administrated containing vaccine name, manufacture, batch number, vaccination date, vaccine labels etc.

v.        Rabies vaccine - depending on local regulations this will be done either 21 or 30 days (EU 21 days and other countries 30 days) (shall be 12 weeks when vaccine administrated).

vi.        RNATT (Rabies blood titer test) – applicable for high rabies countries as classified by destination country (some countries may have a waiting period).

vii.        Internal and External Parasites treatment.

viii.        Screwworm / tapeworm treatment.

ix.        Export permit – not applicable for all countries.

x.        Import Permit – not applicable for all countries.

xi.        COVID-19 PCR test – not applicable for all countries.

Once a guest's submitted documents are accepted and travel is approved, Cargo A&S will notify the contact centre to update the guest's PNR and SSR PETC.

An Electronic Miscellaneous Document (EMD) or Extra Seat for Cabin Baggage (CBBG) will be issued as applicable.

Where Abu Dhabi is a guest's final destination, the UAE Health Certificate must be signed and stamped by a government-accredited health official in their country of departure within five (5) days before their flight.

For all other destinations, guests must complete all arrival formalities according to local regulations.

Where the documents submitted are acceptable and travel is permitted in accordance with the requirements of the applicable countries, Cargo A&S will notify the Contact Centre with an ‘OK 2 Accept’ email..

 

Note: For arrivals into the UAE, the animal’s health certificate needs to be stamped by a government-accredited health official in the country of departure within 24 hours prior to departure; therefore, PETC can be confirmed without the document being provided. Contact Centre staff shall inform the guest that it is a requirement for this signed and stamped form to be carried by the guest and presented at the airport. The 24-hour requirement is applicable for arrivals into AUH (not applicable to transfer between flights at AUH). Individual destination country requirements shall also apply. A fillable and printable PDF version of the form is available on the Etihad.com.

 

Anyone travelling to Abu Dhabi with a pet or service dog must obtain an Abu Dhabi Customs Bill of Entry document at least 24 hours before their departure. To receive it, you need to submit the following documents to NOATUM Logistics:

- UAE residents: Emirates ID copy

- Non-residents: passport copy 

- An import permit for your pet or service dog 

- Your mobile number 

- A copy of your reservation or ticket

 

NOATUM Logistics will review your information and email you the Bill of Entry, which costs AED 365.

 

How much does it cost?

The rates for carrying a pet cat or dog: 

Economy

  • It costs USD 399 or 50,000 Etihad Guest Miles for each way to travel with a cat or dog in Economy

  • If guests are transiting, the combined price of USD 798 or 100,000 Etihad Guest Miles will apply

  • If an adjacent seat booking is requested, it must be done in advance, and guests will be charged for the cost of an extra seat plus USD 399 each way

  • If an additional seat is purchased for a pet, then guests are entitled to the additional check baggage allowance associated with the purchased seat

 

Business

  • As there is no space available under the seat, guests must purchase an extra seat for their pet

  • This must be booked in advance and the guest will be charged for the cost of an extra seat plus USD 399 each way

  • Guests are entitled to the additional check baggage allowance associated with the purchased seat

 

To pay using Etihad Guest Miles, please call us.  

 

c) Falcons in Cabin

Conditions of acceptance

Etihad Airways accepts the carriage of falcons in the passenger cabin for free on all types of aircraft, subject to the following conditions:              

- A valid health certificate and any entry permits required by countries of entry and transit must accompany falcons

- Falcons shall be carried in the passenger cabin at the owner’s risk.

- Falcons must always be hooded and a chain or a rope must be attached to their legs in the passenger cabin or in the vicinity of other passengers in the terminal building etc.  

- The maximum number of falcons carried on any one flight should not exceed 15 on all aircrafts. 

- The maximum journey time must not be more than 17 hours (including transit).                                                                                                          

- Seats are allocated in the last row of the cabin of the ticketed class. If passengers are travelling in groups, they must be seated together. A window seat in the last row must be used for a single passenger with a falcon.

- The falcons and perches are to be placed on the floor area in front of the seat. Plastic sheets should be used to cover the floor area under the falcons and over the adjacent seat. Falcons are not to be placed on the seats. Etihad Airways shall not provide perches. The falcon handler must arrange them. 

- Often VIPs travel in groups, where a number of falcons are carried, accompanied by their handlers. Below seating procedure shall apply to the handler(s) and the falcon(s). 

CLASS

Description

  First/ Business

  Two falcons per guest (per seat) are permitted

  Three additional falcons can be carried for every extra seat paid for

  Economy

  One falcon per guest (per seat) is permitted

  Two additional falcon may be carried for every extra seat paid for

- No extra charges apply for carriage of falcons in cabin

Special requirements:

Falcons are not permitted for carriage to Casablanca (CMN) unless the guest is in possession of a letter of authorisation issued by the Moroccan Ministry of Agriculture. 

When accepted under this exemption, the following documents must be presented:

       1. Valid Health Certificate

       2. Falcon Passport

       3. The Falcon Passport Number must correspond to the same number referenced in the authorisation letter issued by the Ministry. 

 

a) Without an extra seat –

- Create a PNR with the guest’s name and update with SSR FALC.

- The SSR FALC is auto confirmed or declined based on the maximum number of falcons onboard. Once the request is confirmed, travel agents must inform the guest so they can make the necessary arrangements to bring their falcon with them. 

 

b)  With an extra seat (EXST) –

- SSR FALC should be added to the booking accordingly.

- When extra seats are booked, accompanying guests and falcons must be seated together by the Flight Editing team, who will block the last row in each cabin so that these seats are not pre-assigned.

- For ticketing, refer to the EXTRA SEAT (EXST) ticketing policy.

 

 

2) Animal as checked baggage in cargo hold (AVIH)

- Etihad Airways accepts the carriage of falcons in the cargo hold compartment provided that all the necessary health documents and important licenses have been obtained. All other pets are acceptable only as manifested cargo.

- Guide dogs have to be imported into AUH as manifested cargo only, except from USA. However they may be exported as checked baggage free of charge.

 

Conditions of Carriage

- AVIH is not permitted within the cargo holds of the A340 (except for flights to/from USA), A319, and A320.

- For countries known to prohibit the import/export of animals and birds as checked baggage, please refer to TIMATIC/ Embassy concerned.

- All animals and birds should travel as manifested cargo via countries that do not allow the importation of animals as checked baggage.

- Guest must be informed that these animals must be cleared at the cargo terminal upon arrival where they shall be examined by local veterinarian after producing the relevant import and health certificates.

- The guest is responsible for providing all the applicable health documents, declarations and permits as required by governmental regulations of the country to which the pet is to be carried. Container Requirements: Containers used to carry live pets must be clean, leak-proof and escape proof, soundly constructed and in good condition. The size of the container must not exceed the following measurements/dimensions: 135" length x 35" width x 50" height.

- Containers for falcon should allow the pet to stand comfortably.

- Containers for guide dogs to lead the blind or deaf should allow the pet to stand comfortably lie down with paws outstretched and turn around.

Full details of exact container requirements are clearly set out in the IATA Live Animals Regulations manual (LAR section 4). Of particular importance are the restrictions on the size and amount of pets that can be loaded into a container. Specific instructions regarding these limitations are detailed in the IATA Live Animals Regulations manual (LAR) and must be enforced to prevent injury or fatalities to any animal.

 

Role of Reservations & ticketing agents

Brief the guest on conditions of carriage mentioned above.

 

Carriage of falcons

  • Update the SSR AVIH with the number of falcon details
  • Issue an Electronic Miscellaneous Document EMD for “Falcon in Hold” USD 500 is charged per cage per single journey (including transit, if any)

E.g.: Bahrain-Abu Dhabi-Casablanca will cost USD 500, the return flight Casablanca -Abu Dhabi-Bahrain, will be an additional USD 500. Therefore, guest is charged a total of USD 1000 for the entire trip.

 

Carriage of guide dogs

- Update the SSR AVIH details in the PNR with applicable details:

  •     Specify number, type and pedigree
  •     The type of pet (DOG) and breed
  •     The weight and dimensions of the container (Note: these are added as SSR OTHS)

Note: SSR is updated for information only. The documents and cage will be inspected at airport check-in. Carriage may be rejected if the conditions of carriage are not followed.

For more detailed information refer to the Cargo Services Manual or contact the cargo department.

 

 

3)    Manifested cargo

All animals other than the above mentioned, can be transported on Etihad Airways, only as manifested cargo. Guests have to contact Etihad Crystal Cargo minimum 4 working days prior to departure for the carriage of animals (other than Falcons and Guide dogs to lead the blind or deaf).

 

Cargo Contact (in UAE)

Email:                 cargocs@etihad.ae

UAE (Toll Free):    8002535

International:       009712-5091222

For out stations:  Contact local Etihad cargo offices

Guests with allergies and live animals:

Service animals and falcons:

- In Economy Cabin,

o For under-seat carriage, the pet must be able to fit in a pet travel bag or kennel with maximum dimensions of 40 x 40 x 22 cm (L x W x H) to fit safely under the seat.

Terms & Conditions:

Etihad will in this case, not be liable for any resulting costs such as flight rebooking charges, hotel accommodation if Etihad have to refuse the carriage of your pet due to non-compliance with the regulations

- If there are guests travelling on-board that are allergic to animals, our crew may be required to re-seat you and your pet. In rare occurrences, we may need to re-book your flight

- Sedation of animals, except under certain conditions and carried out under veterinary supervision, is not recommended. Commonly used tranquilizers lower blood pressure, which also occurs at high altitude

- The combination of high altitude and medicines could be dangerous for old, chronically sick or stressed animals. Keeping a container in a dark, cool, quiet place prior to flying will calm down most animals. If you have to sedate your pet per veterinarian’s instruction, the name of the drug and time of intake must be clearly marked on the container

In this case, the guest can reach out to our contact centers and request for a refund to the fees that were paid. The guest can request for a full refund for the fees that were paid for transporting the pet if the options that Etihad Airways have provided does not meet their needs, provided that the pet was not transported from the country of origin. If Etihad Airways was able to transport the pet on another flight/date or even airline after obtaining the guest’s consent, then refund is not allowed.

b) Service Animals (dogs only):

This policy is applicable to service animals. A service animal is defined as a dog, regardless of breed or type, which is individually trained to do work or perform tasks for the benefit of a qualified individual with a disability, including a physical, sensory, psychiatric, intellectual, or other mental disability.

 

The following are not considered as service animals:

1. Animal species other than dogs

2. Emotional support animals

3. Comfort animals

4. Companionship animals

5. Service animals in training

 

- Service animals will be accepted free of charge only if they are certified by ADI or IGDF accredited organizations. Only exceptions are guests travelling to/from the USA due to legal requirements.

- Trained service animals must be trained to behave properly in public. The dog must be harnessed, leashed or tethered at all times. They will not be accepted in the cabin if they display any form of disruptive behaviour which may include:

o Growling

o Biting

o Jumping on other guests or staff

o Relieving at the gate or cabin

o Causing damage to the cabin e.g. eating of the seatback

- Guest must request and provide necessary documents to the Contact Centre no later than 48 hours prior to intended travel

- There is no weight limitation for service animal except for Malaysia (up to 8kg)

- The carriage of a service animal in the cabin is permitted on direct EY routes to, from and via Abu Dhabi (i.e. direct transfer)

- It is permitted for a passenger to travel with one (1) service animal in the cabin

- On any flight with falcon(s) travelling in the cabin, a service animal shall not travel in the same travel class as the falcon(s)

- The guest shall provide an absorbent mat to be placed on the floor where the animal will be located and sufficient additional material for the duration of the flight(s) and, where applicable, transfer time

- Where possible, the guest travelling with a service dog should be allocated a bulkhead row and a window seat. Seat will be provided free of charge for a guest travelling with a service animal (SSR SVAN). A guest travelling with a service dog must not be seated in any of the following locations:

o Emergency exit rows

o One row forward and aft of over-wing exit rows

- Service dogs shall remain leashed, harnessed, or otherwise tied at all times. 

- There is no charge for the carriage of a service animal in the cabin

 

 

 Pets and Service Animals

Details are available on the ey.com website. Alternately, guests can call the Contact Centre to enquire regarding travel with a pet or service animal.

Upon receiving a request for carriage of pet in cabin, Guest Contact Centre shall ask some qualifying questions to the guest due to restrictions which may disqualify the carriage of the animal. If any of the below requirements are not met, the guest shall immediately be advised that their animal does not meet the requirements for carriage and to contact Cargo Contact Centre (CCC).

i. Is the animal a trained service dog? If yes, then the Live Animal in Cabin Information Form must be sent to the guest.

ii. For pet cats and dogs, is the animal aged over 16 weeks? If no, then the pet will be rejected (not applicable to service animals)

iii. What is the breed of the pet? If the breed is on banned list, then the pet will be rejected (not applicable to service animals)

iv. What is the weight of the pet including the container? If more than 8 kg, the pet will be rejected (not applicable to service animals except for Malaysia)

v. What are the dimensions of the pet container? (not applicable to service animals)

- Economy: if more than 40 x 40 x 22 (L x W x H), the pet will be rejected.

- Business: if more than 50 x 43 x 50 cm (L x W x H), the pet will be rejected.

If the above conditions are satisfied, Contact Centre staff will provide the guest with:

1. Live Animal in Cabin Information Form

2. Application Form for Trained Service Dog in Cabin (except where the itinerary includes a flight to and/or from the US)

The guest must be advised to email the completed form with the supporting documents to ContactCentre@etihad.ae, no later than 5 days prior to intended travel.

 

Supporting documents:

i. Pet microchip number - must be completed prior to rabies vaccination.

ii. Health Certificate – to be signed by origin approved/government Veterinarian.

iii. Fit to travel certificate - from local vet within 10 days of travel.

iv. Vaccination certificate with all vaccines and treatments administrated containing vaccine name, manufacture, batch number, vaccination date, vaccine labels etc.

v. Rabies vaccine - depending on local regulations this will be done either 21 or 30 days (EU 21 days and other countries 30 days) (shall be 12 weeks when vaccine administrated).

vi. RNATT (Rabies blood titer test) – applicable for high rabies countries as classified by destination country (some countries may have a waiting period).

vii. Internal and External Parasites treatment.

viii. Screwworm / tapeworm treatment.

ix. Export permit – not applicable for all countries.

x. Import Permit – not applicable for all countries.

xi. COVID-19 PCR test – not applicable for all countries.

Once a guest's submitted documents are accepted and travel is approved, Cargo A&S will notify the contact centre to update the guest's PNR and SSR PETC.

An Electronic Miscellaneous Document (EMD) or Extra Seat for Cabin Baggage (CBBG) will be issued as applicable.

Where Abu Dhabi is a guest's final destination, the UAE Health Certificate must be signed and stamped by a government-accredited health official in their country of departure within five (5) days before their flight.

For all other destinations, guests must complete all arrival formalities according to local regulations.

Where the documents submitted are acceptable and travel is permitted in accordance with the requirements of the applicable countries, Cargo A&S will notify the Contact Centre with an ‘OK 2 Accept’ email..

 

Note: For arrivals into the UAE, the animal’s health certificate needs to be stamped by a government-accredited health official in the country of departure within 24 hours prior to departure; therefore, PETC can be confirmed without the document being provided. Contact Centre staff shall inform the guest that it is a requirement for this signed and stamped form to be carried by the guest and presented at the airport. The 24-hour requirement is applicable for arrivals into AUH (not applicable to transfer between flights at AUH). Individual destination country requirements shall also apply. A fillable and printable PDF version of the form is available on the Etihad.com.

 

Anyone travelling to Abu Dhabi with a pet or service dog must obtain an Abu Dhabi Customs Bill of Entry document at least 24 hours before their departure. To receive it, you need to submit the following documents to NOATUM Logistics:

- UAE residents: Emirates ID copy

- Non-residents: passport copy 

- An import permit for your pet or service dog 

- Your mobile number

c) Falcons in Cabin

Conditions of acceptance

Etihad Airways accepts the carriage of falcons in the passenger cabin for free on all types of aircraft, subject to the following conditions: 

- A valid health certificate and any entry permits required by countries of entry and transit must accompany falcons

- Falcons shall be carried in the passenger cabin at the owner’s risk.

- Falcons must always be hooded and a chain or a rope must be attached to their legs in the passenger cabin or in the vicinity of other passengers in the terminal building etc. 

- The maximum number of falcons carried on any one flight should not exceed 15 on all aircrafts. 

- The maximum journey time must not be more than 17 hours (including transit). 

- Seats are allocated in the last row of the cabin of the ticketed class. If passengers are travelling in groups, they must be seated together. A window seat in the last row must be used for a single passenger with a falcon.

- The falcons and perches are to be placed on the floor area in front of the seat. Plastic sheets should be used to cover the floor area under the falcons and over the adjacent seat. Falcons are not to be placed on the seats. Etihad Airways shall not provide perches. The falcon handler must arrange them. 

- Often VIPs travel in groups, where a number of falcons are carried, accompanied by their handlers. Below seating procedure shall apply to the handler(s) and the falcon(s).

Special requirements:

Falcons are not permitted for carriage to Casablanca (CMN) unless the guest is in possession of a letter of authorisation issued by the Moroccan Ministry of Agriculture.

 1. Valid Health Certificate

b) With an extra seat (EXST) –

- SSR FALC should be added to the booking accordingly.

- When extra seats are booked, accompanying guests and falcons must be seated together by the Flight Editing team, who will block the last row in each cabin so that these seats are not pre-assigned.

- For ticketing, refer to the EXTRA SEAT (EXST) ticketing policy.

 

 

2) Animal as checked baggage in cargo hold (AVIH)

- Etihad Airways accepts the carriage of falcons in the cargo hold compartment provided that all the necessary health documents and important licenses have been obtained. All other pets are acceptable only as manifested cargo.

- Guide dogs have to be imported into AUH as manifested cargo only, except from USA. However they may be exported as checked baggage free of charge.

 

Conditions of Carriage

- AVIH is not permitted within the cargo holds of the A340 (except for flights to/from USA), A319, and A320.

- For countries known to prohibit the import/export of animals and birds as checked baggage, please refer to TIMATIC/ Embassy concerned.

- All animals and birds should travel as manifested cargo via countries that do not allow the importation of animals as checked baggage.

- Guest must be informed that these animals must be cleared at the cargo terminal upon arrival where they shall be examined by local veterinarian after producing the relevant import and health certificates.

- The guest is responsible for providing all the applicable health documents, declarations and permits as required by governmental regulations of the country to which the pet is to be carried. Container Requirements: Containers used to carry live pets must be clean, leak-proof and escape proof, soundly constructed and in good condition. The size of the container must not exceed the following measurements/dimensions: 135" length x 35" width x 50" height.

- Containers for falcon should allow the pet to stand comfortably.

- Containers for guide dogs to lead the blind or deaf should allow the pet to stand comfortably lie down with paws outstretched and turn around.

Full details of exact container requirements are clearly set out in the IATA Live Animals Regulations manual (LAR section 4). Of particular importance are the restrictions on the size and amount of pets that can be loaded into a container. Specific instructions regarding these limitations are detailed in the IATA Live Animals Regulations manual (LAR) and must be enforced to prevent injury or fatalities to any animal.

 

Role of Reservations & ticketing agents

Brief the guest on conditions of carriage mentioned above.

 

Carriage of falcons

records.title: Unaccompanied Minors, Accompanied Minors & Younger Passengers (UMNR)
records.html:
When children between 5 and 11 years of age travel alone, we call them “Unaccompanied Minors” (UM), and they are entitled to our UM service. 

For an additional fee, you can request the UM service for children between 12 and 17 years of age. To request this service, parents or guardians must complete the online Unaccompanied Minors booking form.  

 

Unaccompanied Minors (aged 5-11 years)

 

1.      Children aged between 5 and 11 years old are considered to be Unaccompanied Minors (UM).  

2.      Children under the age of 5 will not be accepted as an unaccompanied minor.

3.      Our Unaccompanied Minor service is free for children aged 5 to 11 as long as:

- They are booked on a normal published adult fare

- Booking is created with PTC  (passenger type code) – UNN

- This service has been pre-booked before arriving at the airport.                                                                                

If the service has not been arranged in advance, a fee will apply at the airport.

4.      Occasionally, it may not be appropriate for children with special needs to travel unescorted if the level of care which they require exceeds that which our crew are able to provide. Cabin crew are not permitted to assist in the toilet, administer a guest's medication or feed guests.

5.      The Unaccompanied Minor must be escorted to the airport and met on arrival by the parent or guardian mentioned on the UM form.

6.      The parent or guardian must be present with the child at check-in and ensure that the child has all of the relevant forms and documents to travel alone. Check-in must be completed at least two hours before your child’s flight.

7.      Unaccompanied Minors are permitted to travel on connecting flights operated by Etihad Airways, provided that the transit time does not exceed 8 hours.

8.      Travel on itineraries involving other airlines is not permitted for Unaccompanied Minors. All flights must be operated by Etihad Airways.

9.      Unaccompanied Minors with medical conditions shall be accepted after obtaining medical clearance from Etihad Airways Medical Centre (EAMC).

10.      Unaccompanied Minors are not permitted to sit in emergency exit row seats.

11.       Unaccompanied Minors travelling from Abu Dhabi are not eligible to be checked in from Abu Dhabi and Dubai city terminals.

12.      Etihad Chauffeur and coach services are not provided to Unaccompanied Minors.

13.      Unaccompanied Minors travelling in premium cabins (First or Business) or those eligible for lounge access via an Etihad Guest tier, may not be able to use the lounges in airports other than Abu Dhabi. If the lounge is not operated by Etihad Airways, we cannot guarantee supervision and the level of care, and therefore we may require the guest to report back to the check-in area at a nominated time and be escorted directly to the boarding gate, without lounge access.

14.    The Transit Lounge is available for all departing and transiting Unaccompanied Minors at Terminal A (Zayed International Airport Abu Dhabi).

15.    An Unaccompanied Minor form must be completed in full prior to travel on Etihad Airways operated flights.

16.    At least one copy of the completed and signed Unaccompanied Minor form must be taken to the airport on the day of departure.

 

Accompanied Minors in different cabins

 

Children travelling with parents or guardians on the same flight but in different cabins (for instance, parents travelling in Business and children in Economy), will be considered as 'Accompanied Minors' and treated as 'Unaccompanied Minors' on board the aircraft.

 

1.  Unaccompanied Minors form is not required.

2. The age criteria of our Unaccompanied Minors policy will apply.  Children under the age of 5 will not be accepted as an accompanied minor.

2. Accompanied Minors are permitted to travel on a child fare ticket.

3. The parent or guardian must handle all travel documents for the Accompanied Minor.

4. Guests are requested to limit their visits between cabins during the journey.

5.  If known in advance, update the child’s booking with “SSR OTHS 1A CHD TRVLNG WZ PARENTS IN DIFFERENT CABIN PNR ABCDE”

 

Young Passengers (aged 12-17 years)

 

1.      Young Passengers (YP) between the ages of 12 and 17 are able to travel unaccompanied.

2.      Young Passengers may request our Unaccompanied Minor service for a fee. This service costs US $100 each way on direct flights or US $150 each way for journeys which involve connecting flights.

3.      Young Passengers are permitted to travel on connecting flights operated by Etihad Airways, provided that the transit time does not exceed 8 hours. Travel on itineraries involving other airlines is not permitted for Unaccompanied Minors. All flights must be operated by Etihad Airways.

4.      The Young Passengers Fee applies to all single journeys (inbound and outbound) and is non-refundable.

5.      Occasionally it may not be appropriate for Young Passengers with special needs to travel unescorted if the level of care which they require exceeds that which our crew are able to provide. Cabin crew are not permitted to assist in the toilet, administer a guest's medication or feed guests.

6.      Guests between the ages of 12 and 17 years are not permitted to escort an Unaccompanied Minor. However, legal parents below the age of 18 will be permitted to accompany infants or children with relevant identification.

7.      SSR YPTA (Young Pax Travelling Alone) must be updated in the booking so that these guests can be recognized during disruptions.

 

Country Restrictions:

 

Italian

South African

French

Spanish

Children under 14 must have a completed  Dichiarazione Di Affido and their passport. 

 

- The child may not be allowed to travel if these forms are not completed.

- If the child lives outside Italy, the authorisation can be issued by the Italian Embassy or consulate. 

Children under 18 must have additional documents  and their passport.

 

- Guests can contact the South African Department of Home Affairs on 0800 60 11 90 (toll free from South Africa).

- Alternatively, they can contact their local South African embassy for more details on the requirements.

Children under 18 must have official authorisation   and their passport to exit the country.

 

- The child may not be allowed to travel if these forms are not completed.

Children under 18 must have a signed travel  declaration and their passport.

 

- The permit must be carried in addition to their passport and can be obtained from the Spanish Police, Civil Guard, Courts, Notaries, Town halls or Consulates.

records.title: Indian Goods and Services Tax (GST)
records.html:
Goods and Service Tax (GST) is tax levied on the supply of goods and services by Government of India. Complete information on this tax is available at https://taxinformation.cbic.gov.in

 

GST rule will apply differently depending on whether the passenger is traveling on behalf of a GST registered business (a “Business to Business” or “B2B” transaction), or traveling on his or her own personal account (a “Business to Customer” or “B2C” transaction).

 

The GST will be a dual-administered tax between the Central Government and various States/Union Territories within India, and will consist of several GST rates, including:

- Integrated or Inter-State GST (IGST)

- State GST (SGST)

- Central GST (CGST)

- Union Territory GST (UTGST)

These various rates are harmonized currently, but may vary over time, particularly in the case of the State GST (SGST).

 

Goods & Service Tax (GST) on ticket

- GST shall apply to entire journey originating from India (eg: IXE-BOM-AUH-LHR-AUH-BOM-IXE) irrespective of the country of sale

- The GST rates for air transport are as follows:

o   5% for economy class international travel

o   18% for premium class international travel

- GST applies on:

Ø  Base fare + YQ + YR

Ø  Difference in fare during exchanges

Ø  Change & refund penalty

Ø Booking fee (OB)

Ø  No show fee

Ø  Ancillaries (refer to GST on ancillaries section)

- GST needs to be calculated manually and applied whenever a manual transaction is processed

 

A single interim tax code K3 will be used to collect GST. This tax is to be collected at point of sale and shown separately on the ticket. The selling airline is responsible for remittance.  Penalties will occur if not processed correctly.  This tax is not interlineable. 

 

Exemptions:

 

For economy class Passengers embarking on a journey originating or terminating in an airport located in the state of Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, Tripura or Bagdogra in West Bengal. The exemption applies to/from the following airports: DIB GAU JRH IXI IXS TEZ IMF SHL AJL DMU IXA IXB. However, this exemption will not apply to passengers using the above airports only as transfer points.

 

Regardless of the point of sale and form of payment, an airline must send a GST invoice to a business registered for GST (“B2B” transactions). This invoice must include the GST Number, Name and Address of the business entity registered for GST.

 

These details will differ from the passenger’s own name and address.

- B2B are those passengers who furnish the GSTIN number at time of booking

- B2C are those passengers who do not furnish the GSTIN number at time of booking

 

If a B2B entity does not provide their GSTIN at the time of booking, they must promptly share it with the contact centre via email at contactcentre@etihad.ae within 24 hours of making the booking. Subsequently, the contact centre must update the details in the EY system within 48 hours of receiving the request.

To capture above information, IATA has introduced 4 new Special Service Request (SSR) codes:

 

SSR Code

Description

Purpose

GSTN

Goods and Services Tax Number

To collect the name and registered number of the business purchasing the goods and services.

GSTA

Goods and Services Tax Business Address

To collect the address of the business purchasing the goods and services

GSTP

Goods and Services Tax Business Phone Number(s)

To collect the business telephone number(s) of the business purchasing the goods and services

GSTE

Goods and Services Tax Business Email

To collect the e-mail address of the business purchasing the goods and services

 

- The SSRs GSTN, GSTP, GSTE and GSTA must be entered in the booking before or right after ticketing to ensure the guest receives their GST invoice

- If a guest has not received their GST invoice, it can be downloaded from the following link: https://etihad.supertaxgst.in/guestinvoices

- For any queries regarding invoicing, guests can contact us via email at etihadinvoicing@cnkindia.net. This link and email ID can be shared with the guest as well.

* Refund - K3 tax can be refunded provided the request is made within the cut off dates for the Indian financial year. The financial year runs from 01 April of any given year to 31 March of the following year. The refund cut off is 31 October. e.g. For tickets issued during the financial year 01 April 2023 - 31 March 2024, K3 tax refund is to be allowed till 31 Oct 2024.

This is applicable for involuntary refunds as well as refunds to Voucher/Wallet.

 

 

Goods & Service Tax (GST) on ancillaries

 

K3 will automatically be added to ancillaries when purchased through any of our global contact centres or travel agencies.  However, where the base value is updated manually (e.g. Miscellaneous EMD), K3 must be calculated manually.

- K3 is a percentage-based tax.

- When a journey “originally” originates from India, K3 tax is applicable on the Associated EMDs (EMD-A) linked to any segment in the itinerary (Refer to attached table for K3 applicability)

- For Standalone EMDs (EMD-S), K3 is applicable only on the ancillaries sold in India 

- There are certain ancillaries where K3 is not applicable (Please refer to the table below)

 

For further clarification, see the examples below:

IS K3 APPLICABLE ?

Journey

EMD A 

EMD S

DEL-AUH-JFK-AUH-DEL

K3 tax applies on all associated EMDs sold at DEL / AUH or JFK, since it is related to a journey which originally originates from India (DEL)

K3 tax applies on standalone EMDs sold in DEL or anywhere in India. If a standalone EMD is sold in AUH or JFK, then K3 tax is not applicable

LHR-AUH-COK-AUH-LHR

K3 tax does not apply on associated EMDs sold at LHR/ AUH or COK, since it is related to a journey which originally originates from outside India  (LHR)

K3 tax applies on standalone EMDs sold in COK or anywhere in India. If a standalone EMD is sold in AUH or LHR, then K3 tax is not applicable

BLR-AUH

K3 tax applies on all associated EMDs sold at BLR or AUH since it is related to a journey which originally originates from India (BLR)

K3 tax applies on standalone EMDs sold in BLR or anywhere in India. If a standalone EMD is sold in AUH, then K3 tax is not applicable

AUH-HYD

K3 tax does not apply on associated EMDs sold at AUH or HYD, since it is related to a journey which originally originates outside India (AUH)

K3 tax applies on standalone EMDs sold in HYD or anywhere in India. If a standalone EMD is sold in AUH, then K3 tax is not applicable

records.title: Seat assignment for children under 14 years to or from Canada
records.html:
The Air Passenger Protection Regulations in Canada requires children under the age of 14 years travelling to or from Canada to be seated in close proximity to their parent, guardian or tutor.

 

Guests are able to purchase seats together when they book their flight. We will also do our best to seat families together during check-in at the airport at no extra cost.

 

Policy

- Children four years of age or younger will be seated next to an adult. 

- For children aged five to 14, if it is not possible to seat them next to an adult, every effort will be made to seat them in the same row with no more than one seat between them. 

- If this cannot be arranged, volunteers may be asked to change seats at the airport.

- A free of charge seat will only be offered to the child and one accompanying adult.

- Only standard seats will be provided free of charge.

 

Please contact our Trade Line for seat requests.

records.title: MEDA and Special assistance
records.html:
Special Assistance

 

Guests requiring special assistance should complete a Special Service Request at least 48 hours before their flight.

 

Our crew are fully trained to assist guests with reduced mobility, hearing impairments or vision impairments, and we have a number of wheelchair options available. Please simply request assistance in advance to avoid delays at the airport.

 

Assistive devices such as canes, crutches and foldable walkers are allowed in the cabin, but they must be securely stored before take-off and landing. Cabin chairs are available on board all of our flights to assist non-ambulatory guests to move to and from the aircraft lavatory. The majority of our aircraft are also equipped with accessible lavatories. Electric wheelchairs must be dry-cell operated in order to meet our cabin safety requirements.

 

Guide dogs are permitted in the cargo hold for free as part of checked baggage allowance. All pets must have the correct permits and documentation to travel, and these regulations may vary from one destination to another.

 

Medical Clearance

 

Some conditions may require guests to seek medical clearance before flying.

 

Medical clearance is required if the guest:

·         Suffers from any condition which is believed to be actively contagious

·         Suffers from any condition that may be adversely affected by flying

·         Is likely to be a hazard or a cause discomfort to other guests due to their physical or behavioural condition

·         Is considered to be a potential hazard to the safety or punctuality of the flight

·         Requires special assistance

·         Has recently undergone major surgery

·         Suffers from an unstable physical or psychological condition

·         Requires a stretcher

·         Requires in-flight oxygen, portable oxygen concentrator (POC) or ventilator

·         Requires the use of battery-powered* medical equipment on board (except for CPAP) 

·         Requires a medical procedure during the flight (e.g. injections)

 

*Only dry-cell operated devices are accepted onboard

 

Before a guest receives medical clearance to fly, they must complete and submit a MEDIF (Medical Information for Fitness to Travel) form to the nearest Etihad Airways Ticketing Office or Contact Centre at least 72 hours before their flight. Incomplete forms will not be accepted for assessment. The MEDIF form must be submitted along with a recent medical report from their treating physician (in English). The medical report must have been issued within 14 days of travel.

 

Etihad Airways Medical Centre (EAMC) will determine whether a guest is fit to travel and will notify them if a separate MEDIF is required for the return journey. If approved, EAMC will issue a Medical Certificate through the respective Ticketing Office. Guests may be asked to present the certificate at any time during their journey.

 

Etihad Airways must be notified immediately of any changes prior to travel. In the event that the medical condition changes during the journey, guests will be required to obtain another MEDIF form to continue travelling.

 

Onsite Assessment

 

You can arrange same-day clearance to fly with our fast-track onsite assessment. Our onsite physician will assess guests and determine whether they are fit to fly on the same day.

 

AED1,500 per visit in Abu Dhabi

AED2,000 per visit in Al Ain, Dubai and other locations outside of Abu Dhabi

 

Call +971 600 555 666

 

Nurse On Board

 

Guests with a medical condition can fly with peace of mind thanks to our Nurse On Board service. Our fully-trained nurse will be on hand throughout the entire journey; they’ll ensure that all medical forms and documents are in place, assist with boarding and offer medical assistance during the flight.

 

Call +971 600 555 666 or click here for more information

records.title: Guest Contact Information
records.html:
As per IATA Resolution 830d, from 1 June 2019 we require all travel agents to:

 

  • Actively ask guests whether they wish their contact details to be provided to airlines for the purpose of contacting them in an operational disruption.
  • Update the applicable SSR where the guest agrees to provide their contact information.
  • Advise the guest that they may not receive information from the airline relating to flight cancellation or schedule changes when they refuse to provide contact information. The refusal must be recorded in the booking.

 

Special Service Requests (SSR)

 

IATA has provided SSRs designated for the purpose of capturing the above details in the booking as follows:

CTCE: Passenger contact email address

CTCM: Passenger contact mobile phone number

CTCR:  Passenger contact refused

records.title: Expectant Mother
records.html:
During the first 28 weeks of pregnancy, guests do not need a medical certificate to fly, though we’d always recommend that they speak with their doctor before they travel.

 

Single pregnancy

From weeks 29 to 36, guests will require a medical certificate to fly, which they’ll have to present when they check in at the airport.

At the 37th week of pregnancy, guests will not be accepted to travel.

 

Multiple pregnancy

From weeks 29 to 32, guests will require a medical certificate to fly, which they’ll have to present when they check in at the airport.

At the 33rd week of pregnancy, guests will not be accepted to travel.

 

Medical certificate

Medical certificates must be original and presented during check in at the airport. The certificate must state that the guest is fit to fly, whether the pregnancy is single or multiple, the number of weeks of pregnancy and Expected Delivery Date (EDD).

 

The medical certificate must be:

  • Issued and signed by the treating doctor or midwife within the gestation period considered acceptable for travel
  • Issued on clinic or hospital letterheaded paper or stamped
  • Valid for 3 weeks from the date of issue
  • Written clearly in English or Arabic (other languages are accepted but must be verified by Etihad Airways check-in staff)

With a range of options to enhance their journey, your guests can choose the experience they prefer at a price they can afford.

 

Seating Options

In Economy, your guest can pay for their choice of:

o    Preferred, Exit row and bulkhead seats

o    Economy Neighbor-Free, for more space and privacy (subject to availability)

 

Excess Baggage

Encourage your customers to pre-book their extra baggage online, and save up to 65% on airport fees. To purchase excess baggage, click here.

Note: Discount is applicable 4hrs prior to departure for weight concept routes and 30hrs prior to departure for piece concept routes

Upgrades

Or customers can upgrade to Business or First, and enjoy great food, fully-flat beds or simply more privacy.

 

Lounges

All customers can now access our lounges for a small fee, or organize our personalized Etihad Meet & Greet service to make their journey through the airport even more relaxing.

Etihad Priority Access

Allows customers to:

  • Board the aircraft in the premium queue 

  • Have a priority tag placed on their baggage and delivered first on arrival

     

Policy

  • Etihad Priority Access can be purchased up to 90 minutes before the flight departure 

  • An associated Electronic Miscellaneous Document (EMD) is issued to fulfil the payment

  • A fixed price of USD 50 will apply 

  • The EMD is non-refundable, but it can be refunded if service was not provided, or the guest has been upgraded

records.title: Stretcher Ticketing
records.html:
Guests who require a stretcher booking will be subject to the following policy and procedures:

 

Policy

- Stretcher bookings will be accepted for adults only.

- Guests who must travel in a stretcher onboard must be booked in Economy only and select the number of seats required from six to a maximum of 12 seats.

- Seats will be assigned as per the stretcher configuration table below while booking STCR and non-commercial PNRs (NCP).

- Stretchers will be accepted on Etihad Airways prime operated flights only and not on OAL configured aircraft types.

- Medical clearance must be requested at least 72 hours before the guest's flight.

- Non-medical escorts will be permitted to accompany the guest unless the Etihad Airways doctor issues a mandatory requirement for medical escorts as part of the medical certificate.

- Guests are entitled to the additional check baggage allowance associated with the purchased seats; this will be manually calculated and updated as ‘Itinerary Remarks in the prime booking’ and airports will honour this allowance.

 

 

Procedure

- Stretcher cases are only permitted for travel in the Economy cabin. Specific number of seats (6, 8, 9, or 12) are booked depending on the aircraft type. 

- A single ticket is issued with the adult fare + addition seats. Pricing is manual. 

- The guest is charged the highest Y‑RBD, EY one‑way Deluxe (routing fare) multiplied by the total number of seats booked. 

- A stretcher request can be made only for point-to-point routes e.g. AUH – LHR on EY  

- All applicable taxes must be collected for the stretcher guest. YQ and YR are multiplied by the number of seats; all other taxes are exempt for the additional seats. 

- A Global Service Fee (GSF) will be charged for the stretcher guest only.

- The maximum weight of the guest that can be accommodated on a stretcher is 120 kilos.  

- Tickets can be booked and issued by Etihad Airways agents or Travel agents only.  

- The guest is entitled to the baggage allowance according to the number of seats purchased. However, the total baggage permitted must be manually calculated updated as “Itinerary Remarks in the prime booking”. Airports will honor this allowance. 

- If a booking requires 11 seats, then two NCPs (one for nine seats and another for two seats) must be created to pre-assign seats.

records.title: Extra Seat – Personal Comfort and Cabin Baggage
records.html:
Extra seat – personal comfort (EXST) 

Any guest travelling in Economy who cannot safely and comfortably fit within a single seat with the armrests in the down position is required to purchase an additional seat for their entire journey. This ensures that all guests have access to safe and comfortable seating onboard. Width between armrests are usually 17 inches in Economy.  

 

Guests are required to purchase an additional seat or upgrade if they do not meet the below criteria: 

- Must be able to wear a seat belt, with one extension if necessary 

- Must remain seated with the seat armrests down for the entire flight 

- Must not significantly encroach adjacent seating space  

 

The guest may choose to purchase an extra seat for personal comfort or carriage of pets. 

 

Extra seat - cabin baggage (CBBG)

Guests may book an additional seat if they are travelling with cabin baggage that doesn’t fit in the overhead storage locker.

 

Things to keep in mind

- Guests will be charged the normal ticket fare for the additional seat.

- Only YQ, YR and any percentage-based taxes will be charged - all other taxes are exempt.

- The guest and their extra seat must be booked on the same RBD (Reservation Booking Designator) and PNR.

- This service is only applicable on Etihad-operated flights.

- IATA commission will be as per Etihad’s existing policy in each country of sale.

- A Global Service Fee (GSF) applies only to the guest occupying the seat.

- In case there are any booking changes, penalty charges will apply for both the guest’s ticket and their extra seat ticket.

- Tickets can be booked and issued by Etihad Airways agents or external travel agents.

- If a guest has already purchased a ticket and would like to add an extra seat, the existing booking will need to be cancelled and a new booking of 2 seats (guest + extra seat) will need to be created. To include the fare for the extra seat, the guest's original ticket must be reissued.

- Seats must be assigned at the time of booking. Requests for extra seats can only be accepted if adjacent seats are available on the aircraft.

 

 

1. How to book an extra seat – EXST or CBBG

When creating an extra seat booking, do not start creating a booking with the guest’s profile as this disables the option to select EXST or CBBG. Instead, a PNR for the actual guest and extra seat must be created:

- The first guest's name (name 1.1) must always be the actual guest’s name, followed by EXST or CBBG in the second name field

- Leave the last name blank and enter EXST or CBBG in the first name field

- Do not add a title for EXST or CBBG 

 

GDS Entries for Extra Seat*

 

STEPS

SABRE/ ABACUS/ INFINI

AMADEUS

GALILEO

Create a booking for 2 seats and update the names as

2JONES/ANDREW MR/EXST

NM2SMITH/THOMAS MR(IDEXST)/EXST 

N.2SMITH/THOMASMR/EXST 

N.2ANDERSON/LOUIS/CBBG

SSR for EXST

3EXST/REQUIRED FOR PERSONAL COMFORT-1.2

SREXST-REQUIRED FOR PERSONAL COMFORT/P2

SI.P1/EXST*INJURED PASSENGER

SSR for CBBG

3CBBG/REQUIRED FOR MUSICAL INSTRUMENT–1.2

SRCBBG-REQUIRED FOR MUSICAL INSTRUMENT/P2

SI.P1/CBBG*EXTRA SEAT FOR CELLO

* GDS entries are correct at the time of printing. Please seek assistance from your GDS provider help desk in case of further queries.

 

Using free text in SSR/OSI, it is mandatory to enter the reason for booking the extra seat. 

Examples are given below:

GDS Entries for Extra Seat* 

Sabre – 1S / Abacus – IB / Infini –1F   

 -Assign extra seat to passenger 2 name field -2JONES/EXST 

 -Send SSR to airline 3EXST/REQUIRED FOR PERSONAL COMFORT -2.1                                         3CBBG/REQUIRED FOR MUSICAL INSTRUMENT-2.1 

Amadeus - 1A 

 -Assign extra seat to passenger 2 name field NM2SMITH/THOMAS MR(IDEXST)/EXST   

 -Send SSR to airline SREXST-REQUIRED FOR PERSONAL COMFORT/P2                                                 SRCBBG-REQUIRED FOR MUSICAL INSTRUMENT/P2 

Galileo - 1G 

 -Assign extra seat to passenger 2 name field N.2SMITH/THOMASMR/EXST   

 -Send SSR to airline SI.P2S1.2/EXST*EY EXST REQUIRED FOR INJURED PASSENGER                             SI.P2S1.2/CBBG*EY CBBG REQUIRED FOR CELO 

 

2. Price the extra seat PNR (EXST or CBBG)

- If a guest requests to book an extra seat, they will be charged for both seats.

- The guest and extra seat must be booked in the same RBD (reservation booking designator) and in the same PNR.                                         

- Fare basis should be updated with the applicable booking designator CB for cabin baggage or EX for extra seat (e.g. HHW05V2R/CB).

- A single ticket is issued using double the fare and baggage allowance.

- This request is valid only for PNRs and tickets with EY operated and EY marketed flights and should not contain any Other Airline (OAL), interline or codeshare flights.

- If a guest wants to add an extra seat to an existing ticket, the current booking must be cancelled and a new one be created with two (2) seats; the original ticket may be reissued to include the fare for the extra seat.

- IATA commission is as per the existing EY policy in each country of sale.

- All applicable taxes must be collected; for the extra seat (tickets), only YQ, YR and any percentage-based tax is charged and all other taxes are exempted.

 

3. Ticket the extra seat

Follow the usual steps to ticket the extra seat. Extra seats are not eligible for Etihad Guest Miles.

 

Terms and conditions:

- All items must fit within the allocated seat area without obstructing the aisle; large items, such as musical instruments, may be placed on the cabin floor against the vacant seat and secured with an extension belt, in the bulkhead or behind the lavatory as long as they do not obscure the view to any guest

- Each item must not exceed the following dimensions so as not to obscure any cabin signs, such as seat belt or exit signs:

o Height: 45”/ 114cm (Height can be 61"/155 cm if the guest is allocated a bulkhead seat immediately behind)

o Depth: 9”/ 22cm

o Width: 17”/ 43cm

- The maximum weight of such baggage must not exceed 75kg/165lbs per seat.

- All items should be packaged and/or covered to avoid possible injury to guests or crew.

- All items are subject to security clearance for carriage in the cabin before being brought onboard.

- Cargo and mail will be transported in the cargo hold only.
